artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each complex parameter $\lambda$ in the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, consider the quadratic polynomial
$$P_\lambda(z)=\lambda(z-z^2),$$
which fixes $0$ with multiplier $\lambda$. When $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, the map $P_\lambda$ is said to be linearizable at $0$ if there exists a holomorphic injection $\phi:\mathbb{D}_r\to\mathbb{C}$ with $\phi(0)=0$, $\phi'(0)=1$, defined on a disk of some positive radius $r>0$, such that $P_\lambda\circ\phi(z)=\phi(\lambda z)$; the supremum of such $r$ is called the linearization radius $r_\lambda$ (the conformal radius of the Siegel disk at $0$). For $|\lambda|<1$, $P_\lambda$ has an attracting fixed point at $0$ and one defines $r_\lambda$ as the conformal radius of the immediate basin.

A theorem of Yoccoz asserts that there exists a bounded holomorphic function $U:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that $|U(\lambda)|=r_\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{D}$, and that for $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha$ irrational, $P_\lambda$ is linearizable if and only if $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number. Recall that an irrational $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number if
$$B(\alpha):=\sum_{n\geq 0} \beta_{n-1}(\alpha)\,\log\frac{1}{\alpha_n}<\infty,$$
where $\alpha_0=\{\alpha\}$, $\alpha_{n+1}=\{1/\alpha_n\}$, $\beta_{-1}=1$, and $\beta_n=\alpha_0\alpha_1\cdots\alpha_n$; the function $B$ is the Brjuno function.

By Fatou's theorem the radial boundary values $U(e^{2\pi i\alpha}):=\lim_{r\to 1^-}U(re^{2\pi i\alpha})$ exist for almost every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Question: Does the function
$$\alpha\;\longmapsto\;B(\alpha)+\log\bigl|U(e^{2\pi i\alpha})\bigr|,$$
defined on the set of Brjuno numbers, belong to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})$?
artifact.status_search_result: Yoccoz established that the restriction of $\alpha\mapsto B(\alpha)+\log r(\alpha)$ to Brjuno numbers is bounded above and below by universal constants, answering the boundedness question affirmatively. X. Buff and A. Chéritat (Annals of Mathematics, 2006) strengthened this by showing the function extends continuously to all of $\mathbb{R}$. A finer conjecture of Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz that the extension is 1/2-Hölder continuous remains open, but the boundedness ($L^\infty$) question itself is resolved.

status_evidence.title: The Brjuno function continuously estimates the size of quadratic Siegel disks
status_evidence.snippet: Buff and Chéritat prove that α ↦ Φ(α)+log r(α) extends to a continuous function on ℝ, strengthening Yoccoz's boundedness result.
status_evidence.claim: The function in question is bounded (in fact continuous) on the Brjuno set.

status_evidence.snippet: Yoccoz proved that the restriction of α ↦ Φ(α) + log r(α) to the set of Brjuno numbers is bounded from below and above by universal constants.
status_evidence.claim: Yoccoz proved the L^∞ boundedness of B(α)+log r(α).
